description: How speech is FORMED — the articulatory chain from breath to radiated sound, and the source-filter framework that explains it.

sub_mechanisms.name: respiration
sub_mechanisms.definition: The lungs supply a controlled subglottal air pressure that powers phonation — the energy source of speech; speakers meter exhalation across an utterance.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without the airstream there is no source to vibrate the folds or excite the tract; breath-group structure shapes phrasing.

sub_mechanisms.name: phonation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Vocal folds in the larynx convert the airstream into a quasi-periodic sound source by vibrating; the rate of vibration is the fundamental frequency (F0 = pitch), and whether they vibrate at all is voicing.
sub_mechanisms.why: Phonation creates the harmonically rich VOICED source; its rate carries pitch + intonation, its presence carries the voicing contrast.

sub_mechanisms.name: glottal_source
sub_mechanisms.definition: The excitation feeding the vocal tract: a periodic glottal pulse train (voiced) or turbulent/transient noise (voiceless fricatives, stop bursts). Its spectrum is broadband, falling ~ -12 dB/octave for voicing.
sub_mechanisms.why: The source provides the energy the filter shapes; voiced vs noise source is the deepest production split.

sub_mechanisms.name: source_filter_theory
sub_mechanisms.definition: Speech = a SOURCE (glottal pulse or noise) passed through the vocal tract acting as a linear FILTER. The source sets pitch/voicing; the filter (tract shape) imposes the resonances (formants) = spectral envelope. Source and filter are largely independent.
sub_mechanisms.why: The unifying model of production: it separates what the larynx does (pitch/voicing) from what the tract does (vowel/consonant quality), which is exactly the separation a perceiver must invert.

sub_mechanisms.name: vocal_tract_resonance_formants
sub_mechanisms.definition: The vocal tract is an acoustic tube that resonates at frequencies (F1, F2, F3...) set by its length + constriction pattern; these resonances appear as spectral peaks (formants). Vowels are defined by F1 (height) and F2 (backness).
sub_mechanisms.why: Formants are the primary acoustic identity of vowels + carry place cues for consonants; they are what the filter half of source-filter produces.

sub_mechanisms.name: place_of_articulation
sub_mechanisms.definition: WHERE the main vocal-tract constriction is made: bilabial, labiodental, dental, alveolar, postalveolar, palatal, velar, uvular, glottal.
sub_mechanisms.why: Place is one of the three dimensions that, with manner + voicing, specify a consonant; it is cued acoustically mainly by formant transitions + burst spectrum.

sub_mechanisms.name: manner_of_articulation
sub_mechanisms.definition: HOW the airstream is modulated at the constriction: stop/plosive (full closure + release), fricative (turbulent narrow gap), affricate (stop+fricative), nasal (oral closure + open velum), approximant/liquid, glide.
sub_mechanisms.why: Manner determines the gross acoustic class (silence+burst, aperiodic noise, nasal murmur, formant pattern); it is the second consonant dimension.

sub_mechanisms.name: voicing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Whether the vocal folds vibrate during a segment (voiced vs voiceless), distinguishing pairs like /b/-/p/, /z/-/s/. Cued by VOT, low-frequency periodicity, and F1 onset.
sub_mechanisms.why: The third consonant dimension; together place+manner+voicing pick out a consonant phoneme.

sub_mechanisms.name: voice_onset_time
sub_mechanisms.definition: VOT = the interval between a stop consonant's release burst and the onset of vocal-fold vibration. Negative/short = voiced; long positive (aspiration) = voiceless.
sub_mechanisms.why: The single most-studied phonetic cue; the canonical example of a continuous articulatory timing dimension that perception carves categorically.

sub_mechanisms.name: coarticulation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Articulators move continuously toward upcoming + away from preceding targets, so any segment's acoustics depend on its neighbours (anticipatory + carryover coarticulation).
sub_mechanisms.why: It is WHY there is no invariant acoustic signature for a phoneme — the central source of the variability perception must overcome; also makes speech fluent + fast.

sub_mechanisms.name: syllable_structure
sub_mechanisms.definition: Segments organise into syllables (onset - nucleus - coda) following the sonority sequencing principle (sonority rises to the nucleus, falls after). The syllable is the basic rhythmic + coarticulatory unit.
sub_mechanisms.why: Production + perception are organised around syllables, not isolated phonemes; sonority valleys mark likely boundaries.

sub_mechanisms.name: prosody
sub_mechanisms.definition: Suprasegmental structure above the segment: intonation (the F0 contour), lexical + phrasal stress, rhythm + timing, and phrasing. Carries syntactic, focus, and affective meaning.
sub_mechanisms.why: Speech meaning is not only in the segments; prosody disambiguates, signals structure, and is acquired early (infants track it before segments).

derivation_rules.name: production_consonant_identity
derivation_rules.why: A consonant is specified by the triple place x manner x voicing; perception must recover all three.

derivation_rules.name: production_source_filter_separation
then: pitch is independent of vowel quality
derivation_rules.why: Source-filter theory: the same vowel can be said at any pitch, and any pitch can carry any vowel — they factor.

derivation_rules.name: production_coarticulation_makes_variability
then: context-dependent, non-invariant acoustics for that phoneme
derivation_rules.why: The production-side cause of the perception-side lack-of-invariance problem.
